Book Excerpt

Page 128

EITHER/OR forces us to include at least one of the two things it targets.

Let’s just think through what EITHER/OR means in LSAT terms. It’s slightly different from its real world meaning. I call EITHER/OR an inclusion indicator because it forces us to include at least one option. It does not imply that you can only have one of the pair. EITHER/OR implies that you must have at least one of the pair.

Inclusion Diagramming Process

1. Negate one half of the statement and put it in the sufficient condition.

2. Place the other half of the statement in the necessary condition.
